scope: Batch 5 — Netherlands (van Anraat), Lithuania (Soviet-genocide line), Bangladesh (ICT-BD appellate layer), plus coverage reconnaissance of Ukraine, Croatia, Uruguay and the DRC.

new_case_candidates.case_name: Frans van Anraat (Netherlands — chemical precursors to Saddam's Iraq)
new_case_candidates.country_of_commission: Iraq (Halabja and other Kurdish areas; Iran)
new_case_candidates.crimes: Complicity in war crimes (supply of thiodiglycol for mustard gas); genocide complicity charge acquitted

decisions.reference: Hoge Raad, 30 June 2009, ECLI:NL:HR:2009:BG4822 (on Hof Den Haag, 9 May 2007)
decisions.note: Final cassation confirming the 17-year sentence (reduced by six months for delay). Identity confirmed by procedural fingerprint (born 1942; Hof Den Haag 9 May 2007, 22/000509-06). First-instance ECLI:NL:RBSGR:2005:AU8685 and appeal ECLI:NL:GHSGR:2007:BA4676 also on rechtspraak.nl.

new_case_candidates.note: Major corpus gap: the leading business-accessory case for international crimes, sitting alongside Kouwenhoven and the corpus's corporate cluster (Lafarge, Lundin, Amesys). Related civil litigation involving the Republic of Iraq appears at ECLI:NL:HR:2016:2832 and ECLI:NL:HR:2020:259 — identify before use.

new_case_candidates.case_name: Stanislovas Drėlingas (Lithuania — genocide of partisans, Ramanauskas-Vanagas capture)
new_case_candidates.crimes: Genocide (participation, as KGB officer, in the 1956 capture of partisan leader Adolfas Ramanauskas-Vanagas and his wife)

decisions.note: Plenary cassation ruling: partisans and their supporters constituted a significant part of the Lithuanian national group — genocide conviction stands. Upheld by the ECtHR in Drėlingas v. Lithuania (no. 28859/16, 12 March 2019).

new_case_candidates.note: The affirmative pole of the Baltic Soviet-genocide axis (national/ethnic group 'in part' via political subgroup). Identity confirmed by matching process numbers across both decisions.

new_case_candidates.case_name: Vytautas Vasiliauskas (Lithuania — genocide conviction quashed after Strasbourg)
new_case_candidates.crimes: Genocide (1953 killing of two partisans as MGB operative) — conviction ultimately annulled

decisions.note: Regional-court judgment and Court of Appeal ruling annulled and the case discontinued — execution of the ECtHR Grand Chamber judgment Vasiliauskas v. Lithuania (no. 35343/05, 20 Oct 2015, Art. 7 violation).

new_case_candidates.note: The nullum-crimen counterpoint to Drėlingas — together they map the legality limits of retroactive genocide prosecution. The RIS hits in batch 1's Austrian sweep (Bsw35343/05) are the ECtHR side of this same case.

new_case_candidates.case_name: A.T.M. Azharul Islam (Bangladesh — 1971 international crimes, appellate layer)
new_case_candidates.crimes: Genocide; Crimes against humanity (Rangpur — ICT-BD Case No. 05/2013)

decisions.reference: Supreme Court of Bangladesh, Appellate Division, 14 SCOB [2020] AD 1 (Azharul Islam v. Chief Prosecutor, ICT)
decisions.note: Official Appellate Division text dismissing the appeal against the ICT-BD death sentence.

new_case_candidates.note: Entry point into the ICT-BD appellate corpus on the Supreme Court's own site. IMPORTANT UPDATE TO VERIFY: the Appellate Division reportedly acquitted Azharul Islam on review in May 2025 after the 2024 change of government — the case now spans both the accountability and fair-trial/reversal axes. The ICT-BD line (Sayedee, Kamaruzzaman, Nizami, Mollah) should be retrievable from the same sources in a follow-up pass.

supporting_doctrine.reference: Lietuvos Respublikos Konstitucinis Teismas, ruling of 29 Nov 2010 (byla Nr. 09/2008) on the Soviet-occupation damages and genocide-responsibility laws
supporting_doctrine.note: Constitutional framework of the Lithuanian Soviet-genocide prosecutions (the 18 March 2014 ruling narrowing retroactivity is the companion — search e-tar directly).

coverage_notes: UKRAINE: the indexed Supreme Court layer is dominated by administrative cassation with fully anonymised parties; the art. 438 CC war-crimes verdicts (Shishimarin etc.) live on reyestr.court.gov.ua but cannot be reliably identified through search — source them via the OSCE/ULAG trial-monitoring reports and pin reyestr numbers manually.

CROATIA: the VSRH war-crimes appellate line ('ratni zločin protiv civilnog stanovništva') is richly indexed with official odluke.sudovi.hr links (e.g. I Kž-207/2016-4 of 5 June 2018; Kzz-8/2009-3 of 11 March 2009), but judgments are anonymised — a targeted pass with known case numbers (Glavaš: I Kž-Us 121/2019; Norac/Ademi) is needed to attach names.

URUGUAY: BJN returns only session-based search URLs (not stable document links) and the landmarks (SCJ 365/2009 Sabalsagaray — Ley de Caducidad unconstitutional; the 2010 Bordaberry conviction; SCJ 20/2013) did not surface — keep external sources for Uruguay.

DRC: only the ordinary Cour de cassation/CSJ line is indexed (via Juricaf); the military-court international-crimes judgments (Songo Mboyo, Minova, Kavumu, Kamuina Nsapu) are absent — TRIAL International and Avocats Sans Frontières compilations remain the sources.

SERBIA / BOSNIA / ESTONIA / HUNGARY: not yet swept — candidate veins for a further pass (Belgrade War Crimes Chamber; Court of BiH Section I; Estonian Soviet-deportation cases (Kolk & Kislyiy domestic layer); Hungary's Biszku and Képíró).
